title: Reserve‑anchored soft buffers and priority borrowing — PRD
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Overview:
This PRD describes a new entitlement pattern called 'reserve-anchored soft buffers' and its enforcement surface 'priority borrowing'. The feature lets organizations with reserved capacity allocate a small, managed percentage of reserved compute/usage as an anchored buffer that sibling projects can borrow from under controlled conditions. Borrowing is charged later as overage or auto-rebalanced against other plan reserves depending on policy. The goal is to reduce operational interruptions for enterprise customers who run multiple projects with spiky usage while preserving predictable billing and clear audit trails.

Why this is needed:
- Customers with multiple projects frequently hit transient spikes on non-critical projects and require temporary capacity without immediately purchasing more reserved capacity.
- Current options (hard overage, immediate hard stops, or global bursting) either risk large unexpected bills or service outages.
- A targeted, policy-driven soft buffer with priority weights enables a safer, predictable experience and reduces support escalations.

Principles and constraints:
- Predictable economics: borrowing must be visible in console and on invoices; no surprise charges without prior notice or configured auto-accept policies.
- Auditability: every borrow event must be logged and attributable to caller, route, and project.
- Safety-first defaults: default policy errs on conservative borrowing with early alerts and hard-stop thresholds.
- Backwards compatible: API calls that do not opt into borrowing semantics should behave exactly as today.

Key terms (for this doc):
- Anchor (reserve-anchored buffer): a small percentage (configurable, default 5%) of a reserved plan's capacity that is eligible to be borrowed by sibling projects in the same org.
- Borrower project: the project consuming capacity from an anchor.
- Provider reserve: the reserved plan that owns an anchor.
- Priority weight: integer weight assigned to projects to resolve concurrent borrows (higher => higher priority).
- Safety buffer cap: org-level cap that prevents total borrowed amount across org from exceeding X% (configurable) of summed reserves.

High level UX:
- Console: new 'Anchors' tab under Billing > Entitlements. Admins can enable anchors at the plan level and set: anchor_percent (1-20%), safety_buffer_cap (e.g., 10% of all reserves), default_priority_weight for each project, and auto-accept policy for billing (notify-only, charge-immediately, queue-for-approval).
- API: new endpoints for viewing anchor availability, requesting borrow, and setting per-project priority weights. Borrow requests return immediate token and are tagged with borrow_id for audit.
- Alerts: when a borrow exceeds per-project soft threshold or when projected invoice delta exceeds configured percent, system creates Slack/email alerts and marks route with 'soft-borrowed' status in Console traces.

Enforcement model and rate limits:
- Borrowing is enforced at request routing time. If anchor capacity is available the request proceeds with a borrow token increment. If anchor is exhausted, routing falls back to plan-level policy (hard stop, model downgrade, or queue).
- Per-caller rate limits still apply; borrowed capacity counts toward both the borrower project's quota and toward the provider reserve's anchor consumption.

Billing and reconciliation rules (billing acceptance criteria important):
- Billing representation: Borrow events appear as line items on the monthly invoice under a new section 'Anchor Usage'. Each line contains borrow_id(s), borrower project, provider reserve id, quantity (compute minutes or tokens), unit price (same as overage rate or special anchor rate if configured).
- Charge timing: Two modes supported: immediate-charge (default for self-serve orgs) and deferred-charge (enterprise default). Deferred-charge groups borrow events into a reconciliation bucket and posts a single invoice adjustment at period end with detailed breakdown and per-borrow reference IDs.
- Auto-rebalance: If provider reserves have slack at billing time, the system will consume slack to offset borrows (only if admin opts in). Auto-rebalance is logged as a 'reserve transfer' with zero-dollar internal line items for audit; billing then reflects no overage.
- Refunds & credits: If a borrow was later determined to be misattributed (bug, wrong project), support can create credit using borrow_id references. Credits must reconcile with invoices and be visible in account ledger.

Acceptance criteria (billing and product):
- AC-1: When banked anchor capacity exists on a provider reserve and borrower makes requests, Console shows 'Anchor used: X of Y' in real time within 15s of event.
- AC-2: Borrow requests produce borrow_id and audit log entries including caller identity, route, model, tokens/compute, timestamp, and provider reserve id.
- AC-3 (billing): For immediate-charge orgs, each borrow event for a given billing period is present on the generated invoice as a line item with matching borrow_id(s); invoice generation tests must match ledger totals.
- AC-4 (billing): For deferred-charge orgs, borrow events are aggregated into a single reconciliation line with a broken-out attachment that maps each borrow_id to usage and proposed charge; reconcile action must be visible to admin.
- AC-5: Auto-rebalance only applies when target provider reserve has unused capacity at reconciliation; when enabled, invoice should show zero-dollar reserve transfer entries and no overage for rebalance amount.
- AC-6: Safety buffer cap prevents total borrowed amount across org from exceeding configured cap; attempts beyond cap are rejected and generate alert.
- AC-7: Rate-limit behavior unchanged for non-borrowed requests; borrowing does not allow bypassing per-caller hard concurrency limits.
- AC-8: Support can issue credit/refund by borrow_id with correct ledger adjustments and supporting audit trail.
- AC-9: Drill-down from invoice line item to borrow_id shows console trace (link to request traces) and relevant GitHub PR or deploy tag when available.

API surface (examples):
- GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/anchors -> lists anchors and availability
- POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/borrow -> {project_id, amount, priority_override?} -> returns {borrow_id, accepted, consumed_amount}
- GET /v1/orgs/{org_id}/borrows/{borrow_id} -> details & trace links
Note: these endpoints are additive; existing generation endpoints unchanged. Borrowing tokens are small metadata additions to responses.

Console changes (UX acceptance examples):
- New table in Billing > Entitlements: Reserve name | Anchor % | Used | Available | Safety cap impact | Auto-rebalance flag | Action
- Invoice view: hover over 'Anchor Usage' to reveal collapsible list of borrow_id entries with per-borrow detail and link to request traces

Rollout strategy and canary:
- Phase 1 (internal + selected enterprise pilots): enable anchors read-only (simulate) for 2 weeks while logging events.
- Phase 2 (opt-in pilot orgs): enable borrowing in deferred-charge mode with high visibility alerts and support runbook. Monitor for misattribution.
- Phase 3 (GA): enable immediate-charge defaults for self-serve orgs; enterprise customers default to deferred-charge unless they opt in.

Monitoring and telemetry:
- New metrics: anchor_consumed_per_minute, borrow_requests_per_second, borrow_accept_rate, borrow_reject_reasons, per-org projected_anchor_invoice_delta.
- Dashboards: Billing > Anchors health (consumption, rebalance events, invoice deltas) with 30/90/365 day views.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Console shows anchor usage within 15s for borrow events.
AC-2: Every borrow creates an auditable borrow_id with caller, route, model, amount and provider reserve id.
AC-3: Immediate-charge org invoices include per-borrow line items matching ledger totals.
AC-4: Deferred-charge orgs aggregate borrows into reconciliation bucket with admin reconcile flow.
AC-5: Auto-rebalance only consumes unused provider reserve capacity at reconciliation and is shown as zero-dollar transfers.
AC-6: Safety buffer cap enforced across org and overage beyond cap rejected with alert.
AC-7: Borrowing cannot bypass per-caller concurrency or hard rate limits.
AC-8: Support must be able to credit by borrow_id and ledger must reflect adjustment.
AC-9: Invoice drill-down links to console traces for each borrow_id.
AC-10: Telemetry emitted for every borrow with metrics: borrow_request, borrow_accept, borrow_reject_reason, borrow_amount.
AC-11: End-to-end billing simulation for a pilot org with known volumes matches projected charges within 0.5%.
AC-12: Admin UX allows toggling auto-rebalance and setting anchor_percent, with changes enforced immediately for new borrows.
AC-13: Backward compatibility: systems not using anchor endpoints see no change in behavior or billing format unless they opt in.
edge_cases_and_tests: EC-1: Provider reserve is deleted mid-period: any borrows still map to the old reserve id and become candidates for manual reconciliation; invoice must list them and support must be alerted.
EC-2: Borrower project downscales after borrow: consumption already recorded and billed as usual; refunds require manual credit workflow.
EC-3: Multiple concurrent borrow requests exceed anchor simultaneously: priority weights determine allocation; remaining requests rejected and logged with reason 'anchor-exhausted'.
EC-4: Borrowed amount later found to be misattributed due to instrumentation bug: support credit path verifies borrow_id and creates ledger credit; acceptance criteria AC-8 covers this.
EC-5: Cross-region currency handling: charges converted to billing currency using invoice day FX rate; FX conversion appears on invoice attachment.
EC-6: Org safety buffer cap reached and a new high-priority project requests borrow: system accepts if priority_override configured and admin confirmed; otherwise rejected.
